## Findings
- claim-1: Nonidentity bigrassmannians are parameterized by \(1\le t\le r,s\le n\) with \(t>r+s-n\); \(v_{r,s,t,n}\) is the unique permutation with the stated descent conditions and \(v_t=s+1\), explicitly \[ (1,\ldots,t-1,\ s+1,\ldots,s+r-t+1,\ t,\ldots,s,\ s+r-t+2,\ldots,n). \] [source-2@L973-L993|claim=formal-document]
- claim-2: Set \(i=s-t+1\) and \(j=r-t+1\). The source says \(v_{r,s,t,n}\) corresponds to the \(j\times i\) rectangle \(i^j\); its theorem further assumes \(\schubp_v=s_{i^j}\). [source-2@L1354-L1362|claim=formal-document] [source-2@L1380-L1387|claim=formal-document]
- claim-3: \(\Lambda=\Lambda_{\mathbb Z}(x_1,x_2,\ldots)\); \(I_{r,n-r}\) is the \(\mathbb Z\)-span of \(s_\lambda\) for \(\lambda\not\subseteq(n-r)^r\), and is an ideal. The source gives \[ \Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\cong \mathbb Z[\mathbf x]^{W_J}/\mathbb Z[\mathbf x]^W_+\mathbb Z[\mathbf x]^{W_J} \cong H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z). \] [source-2@L1310-L1330|claim=formal-document]
- claim-4: In the supplied type-\(A\) material, \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) is characterized as the ideal of \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) generated by \[ \{\schubp_u:\Des(u)=\{(r,r+1)\},\,u\ge v_{r,s,t,n}\} =\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(n-r)^r\}. \] [source-2@L1365-L1375|claim=formal-document]
- claim-5: For \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\) and \(b=\min(i,j)\), the theorem labelled `J-generators` gives the two ideal-generating sets \[ \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}, \qquad \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}. \] They generate \(J_v\) in \(H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\). [source-2@L1380-L1402|claim=formal-document]
- claim-6: The source geometrically describes the first upper shape as adjoining an \(a\times b\) rectangle to the right of \(i^j\), top-justified, and the second as adjoining a \(b\times a\) rectangle below \(i^j\), left-justified. It states that each displayed generating set has \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements and degree enumerator \(q^{ij}\qbin{a+b}{a}\). [source-2@L1407-L1421|claim=formal-document]
- claim-7: The formal conjecture is exactly: “The two generating sets for the ideal \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) given in Theorem~\(\ref{J-generators}\) are both minimal.” [source-2@L1489-L1499|claim=formal-document]
- claim-8: The authors report computer verification of that conjecture for all bigrassmannian permutations with \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). This is a reported finite verification, not a proof outside that range. [source-2@L1501-L1502|claim=formal-document]
- claim-9: Separately from the formal conjecture, after setting \(M=J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\), the source conjectures that the abelian group \(M/\Lambda_+M\) requires \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) generators, and further suspects \[ M/\Lambda_+M\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}. \] [source-2@L1536-L1552|claim=formal-document]
- claim-10: The proposition used in the quotient discussion states, for a graded connected algebra \(\Lambda=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\Lambda_n\) and a bounded-below graded \(\Lambda\)-module \(M\), that homogeneous generators of \(M\) correspond to spanning images in \(M/\Lambda_+M\), and inclusion-minimal homogeneous generating sets correspond to inclusion-minimal spanning sets of that quotient. [source-2@L1520-L1534|claim=formal-document]
- claim-11: \(\Lambda_+\) is used in the proposition and in \(M/\Lambda_+M\), but no defining equality for \(\Lambda_+\) appears in the supplied source-2 passages; its intended meaning must therefore remain unresolved here. [source-2@L1529-L1533|claim=formal-document] [source-2@L1536-L1552|claim=formal-document]
- claim-12: The formal conjecture’s word “minimal” is not explicitly defined at its statement. The later proposition explicitly treats “minimal … with respect to inclusion”; this does not by itself identify “minimal” with minimum cardinality in the conjecture. [source-2@L1495-L1499|claim=formal-document] [source-2@L1531-L1533|claim=formal-document]
- claim-13: The related type-\(A_{n-1}\) open question asks for a minimal generating set of \(I_w\), at least for varieties defined by inclusions (reported there as avoiding \(4231,35142,42513,351624\)) or smooth varieties (reported there as avoiding \(3412,4231\)); those subclasses are said there to admit \(n^2\)-element generating sets. [source-2@L1913-L1929|claim=formal-document]
- claim-14: The source generically defines \(W_J\) and \(P_J\) from an arbitrary \(J\subset S\), but the supplied excerpts do not identify the particular \(J\) used for the \(r\)-grassmannian type-\(A\) realization. [source-2@L727-L740|claim=formal-document] [source-2@L1390-L1392|claim=formal-document]
## Strategy
- Specify \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), \(a,b\), and the two Theorem 5.4 sets from the validated locators [source-2@L973-L993], [source-2@L1354-L1362], [source-2@L1380-L1402].
- State \(J_v\) only through its supplied characterization in \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) [source-2@L1310-L1330], [source-2@L1365-L1375].
- Keep distinct: formal minimality conjecture [source-2@L1489-L1499]; quotient generator-number conjecture; stronger free-abelian suspicion [source-2@L1536-L1552]; reported finite computation [source-2@L1501-L1502]; and the separate type-\(A\) question for \(I_w\) [source-2@L1913-L1929].

## Gaps
- No supplied defining locator for \(\Lambda_+\); only its use occurs at [source-2@L1529-L1533] and [source-2@L1536-L1552].
- No independent supplied definition of \(J_v\), \(I_w\), or the particular type-\(A\) parabolic \(J\).
- “Minimal” in the formal conjecture is unresolved: the later proposition addresses inclusion-minimality, not explicitly minimum cardinality.
- Preserve unresolved conventions for empty permutation ranges, zero-exponent partition notation, and the relation of \(|\mu|\) to cohomological degree.
- Record, without correction, the reported apparent \(w/u\) inconsistency at [source-2@L1294-L1307|claim=formal-document].

## Next
- Retrieve exact source-2 definitions of \(\Lambda_+\), \(J_v\), \(I_w\), and the relevant parabolic \(J\).
- Retrieve any source passage resolving the meaning of “minimal” in the conjecture.
- Until then, downstream proof/computation should treat the quotient statement and module structure conditionally on those missing definitions.
